newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaha supplies engine for Ford compact.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha supplies engine for Ford compact.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday it had started supplying new engines to Ford Motor Co for use in a new Ford compact car.
The new engine will be used in Ford's new Puma compact sport coupe which will be produced by Ford in Germany for sale in Europe.

The new engine, called the Zetec-SE, is an in-line four 1.7-litre double-overhead-cam 16-valve, producing 125 horsepower. It features a lightweight compact aluminium cylinder block and a variable cam timing (VCT) system which achieves greater torque and lower emissions, Yamaha said.
Yamaha has not disclosed the volume of engine supplies.
Sales of the Puma will start in Britain this summer and in other European countries from the winter, industry sources said.
Yamaha, which has been supplying car engines to Ford since 1988, now supplies 3.4-litre V-8 engines for use in a sporty version of Ford's Taurus model.
Yamaha also supplies 2.0- and 2.5-litre high-performance engines for use in Toyota Motor's Mark II, Chase, Celica, MR2 and other sporty models.
In 1995, Yamaha provided technical assistance to Ford in Europe, providing engine designs for 1.25- and 1.4-litre engines for use in the Fiesta produced by Ford in Spain.
